READ the list L = {71, 97, 54, 56, 44, 158, 45, 58, 82, 135, 113, 117, 86, 40, 12, 185, 63, 50, 111, 72, 90, 109, 61, 13, 92, 60, 91, 35, 114, 94, 105, 26, 15, 51, 102, 118, 76, 32, 108, 23, 22, 134, 83, 43, 64
CONFIRM that L contains 45 distinct positive integers
NOTE (N=15) indicates that the target number of triples is 15
SET N = 15
DETERMINE whether L can be partitioned into N disjoint triples (a_i, b_i, c_i) such that for each i = 1..N, a_i + b_i = c_i
IF a valid partition exists THEN
OUTPUT one example partition listing each triple (a_i, b_i, c_i)
ENDIF

current_plan.body:
VERIFY that L contains 45 distinct positive integers
SET N = 15
GENERATE all unordered pairs (a, b) FROM L
FOR each pair (a, b) DO
  COMPUTE s = a + b
  IF s IN L AND s != a AND s != b THEN
    ADD triple (a, b, s) TO candidate set
  ENDIF
ENDFOR
BUILD a collection of all recorded candidate triples
SEARCH for a subset of exactly N triples that are pairwise disjoint and together cover all elements of L
IF such a subset exists THEN
  OUTPUT the selected triples
ELSE
  OUTPUT that no valid partition exists
ENDIF
